articles.summary:

The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran's state broadcaster.
US Central Command, which oversees US forces in the Middle East, did not immediately comment.
Earlier Wednesday, Kuwait's Army said its air defences were intercepting drone attacks but did not immediately report any damage. The country's Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated Iranian "criminal" attacks, and said they threatened Kuwait's security and stability.
Iran also recently claimed attacks against US military targets in the tiny island kingdom of Bahrain. Iran targeted US facilities and interests in the neighbouring Gulf countries following the US and Israeli strikes against it on Feb 28.

articles.title: PVR Inox shares jump 6% in 2 days, hit fresh 52-week high as CRISIL upgrades outlook to positive. What is it seeing
articles.summary: Shares of PVR Inox jumped around 4% on Wednesday, extending gains to over 6% in two days after ratings agency CRISIL revised its outlook for the firm’s long-term bank facilities and non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to ‘Positive’ from ‘Stable’.PVR Inox shares hit a fresh 52-week high of around Rs 1,740 apiece on NSE today, pushing its market capitalisation above Rs 17,060 crore. Along with the outlook upgrade, CRISIL Ratings also reaffirmed its 'Crisil AA' rating on the long term debt instruments of the company.Why did Crisil upgrade its outlook for PVR Inox?The rating on the short-term bank facilities and commercial paper programme has been reaffirmed at 'Crisil A1+'. The ratings agency said the outlook upgrade was driven by expectations of sustained growth in the company’s scale of operations across multiple revenue streams and improvement in operating margin strengthening its business risk profile. The outlook revision also accounts for the strengthening of the company’s financial risk profile by becoming a net cash company during the first half of fiscal 2027.Also read | District's PVR INOX ticket sales jump 60%, rivals lag at 4%The structural improvement is driven by PVR Inox’s ability to monetise its network more consistently across content cycles, thereby reducing content concentration risk, Crisil said. It added that the content ecosystem has become increasingly diversified, with admissions being supported by a broader mix of Hindi, regional and Hollywood content. The industry has also witnessed increasing success of mid-budget films which lowers the dependence on a few marquee releases and provides greater stability to admissions and occupancy.Alternate content initiatives such as re-releases, concert screenings, anime content and sports broadcasts have also emerged as supplementary demand drivers and improve utilisation of the existing screen network, Crisil said. It noted that the concerns around OTT-led disruption have also moderated as the theatrical-first release model has been re-established, with producers increasingly using theatrical performance as the primary benchmark for content monetisation on OTT, highlighting the complementary nature of theatrical and digital channels.PVR Inox’s business risk profile is also supported by increasing geographical diversification as the company continues to expand its presence in southern India and tier 2 and 3 markets, which benefit from strong movie-going culture, multiple thriving film industries and relatively low multiplex penetration, the ratings agency said, further noting that the company’s screen portfolio in southern markets increased from 31% at the end of fiscal 2023 to 34% in at the end of first half of fiscal 2027, with more than 35% of screen additions over the past three years originating from the region. “This diversification supports admissions visibility and reduces dependence on any single language or regional content cycle,” it said.Crisil further highlighted PVR Inox’s earnings, pointing out that the company demonstrated healthy revenue growth driven by a mix of increasing admissions, increasing average ticket prices (ATP), higher spends per head (SPH), and improving monetisation of its customer base. Net debt reduced, aided by strong accrual generation and proceeds from the divestment of the 4700 BC business for about Rs 227 crore in January 2026. Despite completion of a Rs 300 crore maiden share buyback in the first half of fiscal 2027, leverage metrics are expected to remain comfortable, the ratings agency said. It expects the company’s net worth to remain healthy and gradually improve over the medium term, supported by strong accrual.“The ratings reflect the company’s strong market position with an established brand, expectation of further improvement in operating efficiency, led by synergistic benefits and premiumisation, and a strong financial risk profile. These strengths are partially offset by inherent volatility of the film exhibition business with operating performance remaining dependent on the quality and timing of content releases and evolving consumer preferences,” it said.Also read | PVR INOX bets on smaller multiplexes as single-screens declinePVR Inox share pricePVR Inox shares jumped more than 9% in a week and 23% in a month. This comes amid blockbuster releases including Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Part 1. The stock has so far gained more than 70% in 2026.The shares of the multiplex chain operator have delivered 55% returns over one year. articles.summary: A federal judge on Tuesday blocked President Donald Trump's administration from restricting the types of internships and other practical training opportunities available to international students attending US universities on visas.US District Judge Julia Kobick in Boston issued an injunction barring the US Department of Homeland Security from enforcing two August directives that higher education groups said had abruptly disrupted training opportunities for foreign students nationwide.Kobick, an appointee of former Democratic President Joe Biden, ruled in a lawsuit filed last month by four organizations, including the Association of American Universities and the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration.It marked the latest victory for plaintiffs challenging efforts by the Trump administration to impose restrictions on student visa holders as part of its hardline immigration agenda. On Monday, a different federal judge in Boston struck down a new rule that would limit how long ‌foreign students can remain in the US without applying for extensions.DHS declined to comment.The education groups in the case before Kobick argued that DHS had sharply narrowed rules that for more than 35 years governed international students' participation in internships and other practical training through a program known as curricular practical training, or CPT.They said foreign students historically could take part in school-authorized internships and training opportunities as long as they were directly related to their field of study and formed an integral part of an established curriculum.According to the plaintiffs, the government long interpreted that standard to allow participation when training either carried academic credit or was required to earn a degree.Amazon and Tesla were the top two employers of CPT students in 2024, when 140,775 student visa holders were authorized to participate in CPT overall, according to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.But in August, DHS, which oversees ICE, issued messages telling universities that internships and other opportunities qualified only if they were mandatory for every student in a degree program and did not cover elective training taken for academic credit.The agency said it had seen an increase in CPT authorizations it believed did not comply with program requirements and would increase scrutiny of approvals.Kobick found the directives were likely arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act as DHS had failed to acknowledge that it was making a "fundamental" change to the government's longstanding interpretation of the program's rules."Correct or not, this new interpretation is inconsistent with the government's previous position," she wrote.

articles.summary:
Wheat - the main rabi crop - has been sown on 50.07 lakh hectare so far this year, down by 15.27 per cent from 59.10 lakh hectare a year ago, according to data released by the Union Agriculture Ministry.
The wheat crop is usually sown in October-November and harvested in March-April. In the 2025-26 crop year (July-June), wheat was planted on 336 lakh hectare.
As per the latest data, the pace of wheat sowing is lagging behind as compared to last year due to the 13 per cent deficient June-September monsoon, which reduced residual soil moisture before sowing began.
Experts said lower irrigation availability is another factor, with reservoir and canal water levels below normal in key wheat-growing states. Wheat requires several rounds of irrigation after planting.

articles.title: Nvidia shares crash 24% amid Huang scandal. Why UBS sees 54% upside
articles.summary: Shares of Nvidia have plunged around 24% since the start of the month, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market value amid controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's alleged extramarital affair with a Chinese spy and his subsequent resignation. However, UBS has sought to allay investor concerns, pointing to attractive valuations following the sharp selloff.While many analysts are sounding the alarm over Nvidia’s future, UBS thinks the assumptions are brutal and unlikely to be correct, given the chip giant's momentum for at least two more years, even without Huang as CEO, Yahoo Finance reported. In essence, the market assumes that 2028 will be the peak for Nvidia, with no growth thereafter and EBITDA margins compressing by 1,500 basis points, UBS analyst Tim Arcuri wrote on Monday. "This seems incredibly draconian to us."Nvidia valuations after selloffThe UBS analyst believes that the near-term damage to the stock has been done. He believes that it doesn't make sense to give up on the stock after being down this much especially ahead of January hyperscaler earnings calls where the international brokerage thinks capex will be guided higher than current Street expectations.UBS maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Nvidia shares but reduced its target price to $240 apiece from $300 per share. The latest target price still implies around 54% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of $156.14 apiece.Also read | Nvidia board not considering Jensen Huang's return as CEO, focuses on probe: ReportBank of America analyst Vivek Arya, as quoted by the report, also feels that the stock has become sharply cheap after the selloff. He noted that 11x forward PE is a multi-decade low and a 36% forward discount to close peer Broadcom, reflecting a considerable amount of stress and potential for rebound.All eyes on Nvidia earningsNvidia is all set to announce its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, with investors eagerly awaiting the chipmaker’s results after Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy and his subsequent resignation sparked a massive 24% plunge in the stock this month so far.The Q3 earnings print would mark the first quarterly results announcement without Huang at the helm of the chipmaker. He resigned as the CEO of the company last week, following which Nvidia's finance chief, Colette Kress, took charge as the interim CEO. Its board has said it is in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role.Nvidia’s earnings also come at a critical juncture in the AI trade. Earlier this year, chip linked stocks rallied sharply as hyperscalers spiked their AI spendings and new innovations related to the nascent technology came to light. However, analysts soon began to question the massive capex plans and whether they will actually bear fruits in future, leading to an equally sharp downturn in the stocks that rallied during the frenzy.Nvidia is seen as one of the faces of the artificial intelligence-led boom.
